Today’s big headlines in 5 minutes: Your quick brief on politics, national and global events, entertainment, and sports.
Good morning, readers! Here are the top headlines from the day that you need to know - from politics and world news to sports and entertainment.
Trump, Xi, Putin set for historic meet today
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold a trilateral meeting on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen.
The trilateral meeting is expected to take place on Thursday on the sidelines of the Apec leaders' summit in the southern Chinese city. China said the three leaders will hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations". Track latest and LIVE updates here
Slain terrorist Lateef Bhat's funeral held amid tight security
Deep Dive
Around 10pm on Wednesday, nearly 160km from the one-storey house of slain Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat, his body was buried by family members in the presence of security forces.
In keeping with the government’s policy of not handing over the bodies of slain terrorists to their families to prevent public funerals and the glorification of militants, Bhat’s family was taken to a village in the Bangus valley of Jammu and Kashmir’s Kupwara district for the burial. The family lives in Khrewan village in Kupwara. Read the full story here.
Grand Theft Auto VI arrives in record-shattering media release
The world has just witnessed the biggest entertainment release in history — and it isn’t a Hollywood movie. Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI began rolling out for users on Wednesday evening, as the global release of the long-awaited video game capped a protracted eight-year development saga.
But even before consoles around the world began booting GTA VI — the game was released for Indian users at midnight on Thursday — it had made more money than any film has ever earned in its opening weekend. Rockstar Games’s follow-up to GTA V had booked about $1.5 billion — roughly ₹14,100 crore — in pre-orders by Wednesday, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. Avengers: Endgame, which holds the record for the biggest global opening in cinema history, made $1.2 billion in its first weekend in 2019. Read the full story here
Cyclone Akvan advances; landfall likely between Andhra and Odisha tomorrow
Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan moved northwards at a speed of 5 kmph over the west-central and adjoining central parts of the south Bay of Bengal during the six hours ending 11.30 pm on November 18, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
As per IMD, the landfall is expected to take place tomorrow - November 20 near Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. Follow LIVE updates here
India vs New Zealand Test Day: Nicholls, Phillips fifties bring Kiwis back into game after early Bumrah damage
India made a strong start to the opening Test against New Zealand, reducing the hosts to 60/4 at lunch on Day 1 in Wellington. Jasprit Bumrah led the attack with two wickets, while Anshul Kamboj, and Akash Deep taking once wicket each.
Bumrah and Kamboj put the openers back in the pavillion inside 4 overs, before Henry Nicholls and Rachin Ravindra steadied the ship with a 39-run stand. Just before lunch, India struck twice in quick succession. Track the LIVE updates here.

morning.text:
Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, senior executives to visit Air India’s Gurugram headquarters
The visit comes as the airline works to turn around its business years after the Tata Group acquired it in January 2022
Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata and members of the conglomerate’s board are scheduled to visit Air India’s headquarters in Gurugram on Thursday, people familiar with the matter said. The visit comes as the airline works to turn around its business years after the Tata Group acquired it in January 2022.
“Noel Tata and senior management of Tata Sons are to visit both the airline headquarters and its academy,” said one of the people. A second person said the board members are expected to review the airline’s performance as it continues to make losses.
The people said senior executives visiting Air India’s headquarters may include Tata Sons chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran.
Noel Tata was unanimously appointed chairman of Tata Trusts in October 2024, two days after his half-brother Ratan Tata died. The appointment put him at the helm of the philanthropic institutions that collectively own about 66% of Tata Sons.
Noel Tata has differed with the Tata Sons board over the reappointment of Chandrasekaran for another five-year term, a planned public offering of Tata Sons, and growing losses in new-age businesses including aviation, electric vehicle batteries, digital commerce and semiconductors.
The visit of the senior executives to Air India’s headquarters comes against the backdrop of the airline’s announcement last month that it would establish a full-time team to systematically review expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities, attempting to embed cost consciousness, frugality and disciplined decision-making into its culture.
In his first internal communication to airline employees, seen by HT, Air India’s chief executive officer (CEO) Tewolde Gebremariam in October said cost savings could not be driven by a single team or function and required the active participation and commitment of every employee.
“Cost consciousness must become part of our culture,” Gebremariam said. He added that alongside operational excellence, the airline needed to embed “a mindset of frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making in everything we do”.
The focus on costs came as airlines continue to operate in a challenging environment, with elevated oil prices amid the West Asia crisis and pressure on fuel bills, margins and flight routes.
Tewolde said small decisions, taken consistently across the organisation, can collectively strengthen the airline’s financial resilience. He announced a cross-functional Cost Savings Team had been established on a full-time basis to identify cost-saving opportunities across the organisation.
A multidisciplinary team was established to support this effort. The team, he said, will systematically review all expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities across functions.
Gebremariam asked employees to extend their “full support and cooperation” to the team as it works to deliver cost efficiencies across the organisation.

morning.text:
Over 17,000 end of life vehicles seized in Delhi till Nov 2: Traffic police data
To encourage people to surrender such vehicles and scrap them only at authorised facilities, the Delhi Traffic Police launched a special drive named “EOL Vehicles Awareness Mela”
Over 17,000 end of life vehicles (EOL) were seized between January 1 and November 2 this year, data shared by Delhi Traffic Police revealed. Of them 16,918 were two-wheelers, while 164 were cars. The remaining vehicles were three-wheelers and others.
To encourage people to surrender such vehicles and scrap them only at authorised facilities, the Delhi Traffic Police launched a special drive named “EOL Vehicles Awareness Mela”.
During this drive between November 12 and 16, as many as 240 end-of-life vehicles, which completed their life span of ten years as diesel and 15 years as petrol vehicles, were impounded and later sent for scrapping after their owners surrendered them during the special drive, said additional commissioner of police (ACP) (traffic) Vijayanta Goyal Arya.
Also Read: Over 4.5 lakh PUC challans issued in Delhi till Oct 27: Traffic police data
She added that nearly 5,000 people attended the awareness programme organised at multiple locations across central, eastern and northern traffic ranges, which fall under Zone-1 traffic, during the four days.
“It’s a new initiative undertaken in Zone-1 traffic with the objective of promoting a cleaner, safer and pollution-free Delhi. Keeping in mind the positive outcome of the awareness programme, we plan to launch it in the entire city,” said Arya.
During the awareness drive, citizens were educated about the rules governing EoL vehicles and the environmental concerns associated with their continued use. They were also guided on how to dispose of such vehicles through authorised scrapping facilities. Through the EoL Vehicles Awareness Mela, which also included representatives from the Delhi transport department, thousands of citizens—including members of residents’ welfare associations (RWAs) and markets’ welfare associations (MWAs) across central, eastern and northern areas of Delhi -- were briefed on the legal consequences of using EoL vehicles, the benefits of authorised scrapping and the importance of removing abandoned vehicles from residential areas and public spaces.
“Traffic personnel and transport department representatives urged the public to avoid dealing with unauthorised scrap dealers for scrapping their EoL vehicles. RWAs and MWAs were encouraged to help spread the message and support removing abandoned vehicles, which can obstruct traffic and affect public safety and cleanliness.
“The Zone-1 traffic police personnel have impounded 9,916 EoL vehicles so far,” Arya added.

morning.title: Shashi Tharoor-led Parliamentary panel to discuss India-Pakistan relations
morning.text:
Shashi Tharoor-led Parliamentary panel to discuss India-Pakistan relations
The Tharoor-led external affairs committee has decided to discuss "Recent developments in India-Pakistan Relations" as one of the 18 subjects it will take up
A Parliamentary panel has decided to review India-Pakistan relations, a subject of immense significance, especially in the wake of Indian forces' targeting of terrorist launch pads and military installations deep inside Pakistan for the first time during Operation Sindoor.
India carried out Operation Sindoor in May last year following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that left 26 civilians dead.
The Shashi Tharoor-led external affairs committee has decided to discuss "Recent developments in India-Pakistan Relations" as one of the 18 subjects the panel will take up over the next year.
According to functionaries, foreign secretary Vikram Misri is likely to brief the panel on the issue.
In June, Misri had briefed the panel on a similar issue with special reference to the India-Pakistan border. Still, the meeting was a precursor to the panel's study visit to Jammu, Srinagar, Kargil and Leh from June 22 to 25. A senior functionary said the upcoming discussion on India-Pakistan ties is set to be more detailed, as it will be a standalone subject.
Over the past few years, the relations between the two neighbours have further strained, with India refusing to engage in any diplomatic discussions till terror ends. New Delhi placed in abeyance the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably ends its support for cross-border terrorism; the Attari border was closed, and bilateral trade was embargoed.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said in his address to the nation at the time, "trade and talks cannot go on simultaneously. Terror and trade can't go on, and water and blood can't flow together," setting the new normal between India and Pakistan.
In recent times, Tharoor has written on the India-Pakistan issue on several occasions. In an article in AsiaLink on October 10, Tharoor said that the current stalemate should not be seen as a pause between rounds of negotiation, but as a deliberate strategy of disengagement.
He maintained that until Pakistan's security calculus is altered through a political transformation, the silence across the subcontinent will endure—and the risk of catastrophic error will remain.
Operation Sindoor and aftermath
Operation Sindoor, a precision military strike on May 7, 2025, targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, responding to the Pahalgam attack that killed 26 people. The operation aimed to dismantle networks tied to Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba.
Escalating cross-border hostilities, including drone attacks, missile intercepts, and retaliatory strikes, had sharply raised tensions.
After the operation was suspended, the PM had said, "Operation Sindoor is India's policy against terrorism. It has carved out a new benchmark in our fight against terrorism and has set up a new parameter and new normal."
"First, if there is a terrorist attack on India, a fitting reply will be given. We will give a befitting response on our terms only. We will take strict action at every place from where the roots of terrorism emerge. Secondly, India will not tolerate any nuclear blackmail. India will strike precisely and decisively at the terrorist hideouts developing under the cover of nuclear blackmail. Thirdly, we will not differentiate between the government sponsoring terrorism and the masterminds of terrorism," he added.

morning.text:
MCD schools to introduce QR code system, move admissions online
The civic body said it will also launch an online registration facility through its EduLife portal to simplify and digitise the admission process
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has introduced a QR code-based system to increase enrolment in its schools. The civic body said it will also launch an online registration facility through its EduLife portal to simplify and digitise the admission process.
“The MCD’s education committee decided that a QR code be installed outside every MCD school. Parents will be able to scan the QR code and submit their details. The concerned school principal and teachers will then contact the parents and complete the admission process for their children,” the civic body official said.
To ensure proper monitoring of the online registration process, the MCD said it would appoint a nodal officer at the Civic Centre. The officer will be responsible for forwarding applications received through the portal to the nearest school in the respective area. The school authorities and teachers will then contact the parents and complete the admission formalities.
Also Read:MCD plans 24 ‘Nigamshree Schools of Excellence’ to improve civic school education
According to official data, student enrolment in MCD schools has declined steadily over the past five years, from around 8.17 lakh in 2022-23 to 7.92 lakh in 2023-24 and 7.86 lakh in 2024-25.
The figure further dropped to 6.40 lakh in 2025-26 and approximately 6.2 lakh in 2026-27.
The civic body also said it was fast-tracking the recruitment of around 3,000 sanitation workers and security guards, and regularising existing workers at the earliest. It has also directed the horticulture department to draft a proposal for the appointment of staff to ensure upkeep of the schools park and playground.

“The additional commissioner of the MCD has been asked to expedite the file related to the recruitment of approximately 3,000 sanitation workers and security guards within one week,” the official added.
“The horticulture department was directed to prepare a proposal for the appointment of maintenance staff and gardeners on the basis of the prescribed yardstick where children can have access to clean, well-maintained parks and better sports facilities,” the official added.

morning.text:
Elephant linked to 16 deaths tranquilised, fitted with satellite radio in Chhattisgarh
Around 200 forest personnel were deployed to track the tusker.
An elephant that is linked to the deaths of 16 people across Chhattisgarh districts was tranquilised, fitted with a satellite radio collar and released into the forest on Wednesday, officials said, as human-animal conflict rises in the state.
The elephant, locally known as ‘Kabra Kaan’ because of its patchy ears, has been blamed for the deaths of 16 people in Surajpur and adjoining Balrampur districts over the past six to seven months.
“The team had been monitoring the elephant’s movement and waiting for a suitable opportunity to tranquilise it. The elephant has now been fitted with a satellite radio collar and released into the forest,” said Pranay Mishra, Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF), Surguja range.
According to forest officials, the elephant had been moving across forest areas under Pratappur, Ghui, Surajpur, Rajpur, Ambikapur and Tamor Pingla ranges, posing a threat to human life and property. Around 200 forest personnel were deployed to track the tusker. The radio collar will help officials monitor its movements and alert villagers about its presence.
The latest death of a 45-year-old woman was reported in Umeshwarpur village under Premnagar area of Surajpur district last Wednesday. The elephant was spotted in the area around 11 pm.
The forest department had secured approval from the Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) to tranquilise the elephant and fit it with a satellite radio collar. The Divisional Forest Officers of Surajpur and Balrampur were appointed joint nodal officers to oversee the operation, with veterinary doctors and senior forest officials assigned to assist the team.
Officials had also considered deploying trained captive elephants, known as kumkis, if required for the operation.

morning.text:
MCD plans 24 ‘Nigamshree Schools of Excellence’ to improve civic school education
These will not be newly established institutions but existing MCD schools identified for their potential to develop into high-performing schools
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is planning to develop 24 existing schools as ‘Nigamshree Schools of Excellence’, which will serve as model institutions and mentor neighbouring civic schools. The proposal, moved by the MCD education department and recommended by the civic body’s education committee, envisages selecting two schools in each of the corporation’s 12 zones in the first phase.
These will not be newly established institutions but existing MCD schools identified for their potential to develop into high-performing schools, officials said.
The initiative comes against the backdrop of challenges faced by the civic school system, including inadequate infrastructure and concerns over student enrolment. The proposal acknowledges the need to establish clear benchmarks for teaching, school leadership, infrastructure and community participation, while rebuilding public confidence in MCD schools.
Under the plan, the 24 selected schools will function as resource and mentoring centres, providing academic guidance, sharing learning resources and demonstrating effective teaching practices to three to five nearby MCD schools each.
The aim is to use the initiative as a catalyst for improvement across the wider school network, which caters to around seven lakh students, according to the proposal.
“The schools will be required to meet a set of infrastructure standards, including at least two smart classrooms, functional internet connectivity, computer laboratories, CCTV cameras, smart boards or smart televisions, and dedicated libraries with age-appropriate books. They will also need adequate classrooms, safe drinking water, functional toilets, separate facilities for boys and girls, and accessible infrastructure for children with special needs,” official said.
Also Read: MCD sets target of 50,000 fresh admissions in its schools in a month
Once these benchmark schools are set up, the department will try to replicate the model in other schools.
The proposal also envisages playgrounds, sports equipment, activity spaces, green campuses and adequate teaching and support staff.
“Experienced teachers and school heads with a record of academic and administrative performance will be prioritised. School leaders will also undergo at least 50 hours of annual professional development training,” the policy states.

morning.title: Slain terrorist Lateef Bhat's funeral held amid tight security, 160 km away from his village
morning.text:
Slain terrorist Lateef Bhat's funeral held amid tight security, 160 km away from his village
HT spoke to Lateef Bhat's family members, who confirmed that the body was buried nearly 4 hours away from their house, following faith and customary rituals
Around 10pm on Wednesday, nearly 160km from the one-storey house of slain Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat, his body was buried by family members in the presence of security forces.
In keeping with the government’s policy of not handing over the bodies of slain terrorists to their families to prevent public funerals and the glorification of militants, Bhat’s family was taken to a village in the Bangus valley of Jammu and Kashmir’s Kupwara district for the burial. The family lives in Khrewan village in Kupwara.
In the past, the killing of terrorists, insurgents and Naxals in security operations has often been followed by large public funerals.
Deep Dive
HT spoke to Bhat’s family members, who confirmed that the burial took place nearly four hours’ drive from their home. They said the funeral was conducted according to religious and customary rituals, but without mobile phones or photography, in the presence of security personnel.
Bhat’s maternal uncle, Mohammed Altaf, who spoke to HT while returning from the funeral, said eight male family members attended the burial. Altaf confirmed that all the customary funeral rites were performed.
“We were not allowed to take photographs. Security forces took our phones about 10km away before driving us to a cemetery in a village in Bangus, Handwara, Kupwara district. I was there along with his father, Mustaq Ahmed Bhat, two maternal uncles, his three paternal uncles and one brother-in-law. He is buried there,” he said.
Centre's policy on terrorist dead bodies
The Centre has reiterated on several occasions that it would not hand over the bodies of slain terrorists to their families.
“Now, wherever a terrorist is killed, he is buried right there. In Narendra Modi’s rule, there is no permission to take out a funeral procession to glorify any terrorist,” Union home minister Amit Shah said in the Lok Sabha on June 29, 2025, during a special discussion on India’s successful Operation Sindoor.
Last year, when Maoist leader and CPI (Maoist) chief Nambala Keshava Rao, alias Basavaraju, was killed, his body was cremated in Bastar and not allowed to be transported to his hometown in Andhra Pradesh.
There have been similar instances in the past. Afzal Guru, convicted in the 2001 Parliament attack case, was buried inside Delhi’s Tihar jail after his execution. His body was interred in an area of the prison that is out of bounds for inmates. Tihar jail also houses the grave of separatist Maqbool Bhat, who was executed there in 1984.
Kulgam encounter
22-year-old Mohammed Lateef Bhat, a local Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist commander described by the Union government as the terror outfit's last known active local recruit in Jammu and Kashmir, was killed in an encounter with security forces in Kulgam on Wednesday, police said. For the last week, since the attack on 3 CRPF personnel, who sustained bullet wounds and are recuperating, a joint team of security forces led by the Indian Army's Victor Force under the 9 Rashtriya Rifles (RR) had been leading the operations to find Bhat.
The Victor Force is the RR's counter-insurgency unit in J&K.
The forces had rounded up hundreds of people and were conducting door-to-door searches. On Wednesday morning, when he was traced to a location, Bhat refused to surrender despite video calls by the police and was later shot dead.
At around noon, Altaf, along with Bhat's father, Mushtaq Bhat and other family members, was allowed to leave an interrogation centre where they had been questioned and housed since the attack on the CRPF personnel on November 11. They were first taken to Srinagar, a medical facility of the security forces where the body had to be identified. Bhat's father identified the body as his son, whom he had reported missing a year ago.
In the last year, Bhat has been involved in two terror attacks - the murder of a J&K police official and the killing of two migrant workers from Chhattisgarh. The family said they had not heard from Bhat for the last year, but a close family friend denied this and claimed that Bhat had come to the Khregan village sometime in July (after he had joined the terrorist outfit but was yet to execute the twin terror attacks).

morning.text:
Odisha evacuates 46k people as cyclone Akvan approaches; red alert for 11 districts
The state government stepped up preparedness measures as Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi held a high-level meeting/
Over 46,700 people in Odisha have been evacuated to safer locations as severe cyclonic storm 'Akvan' over the westcentral Bay of Bengal lay centred about 580 km south of Gopalpur and 640 km south of Puri at 2.30am on Thursday, officials said.
The cyclone is likely to make landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in the eastern state on Friday. A clearer picture of the storm's trajectory and likely impact is expected by Thursday as its speed and direction continue to change, the officials added.
The storm, according to India Meteorological Department (IMD), was also located about 470 km east-southeast of Narsapur and 490 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, and 570 km east-northeast of Chennai.
Deep Dive
"Odisha's south and northern region along with coastal parts is likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall and, at places, extremely heavy rainfall on Friday and Saturday," IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said.
The state government stepped up preparedness measures as Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi held a high-level meeting on Wednesday. At least 14 districts – Gajapati, Ganjam, Puri, Khurda, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, Balasore, Nayagarh, Cuttack, Jajpur, Dhenkanal, Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj – are likely to be affected by the cyclone and associated rainfall.
The government has issued a red alert for 11 districts, with Ganjam, Malkangiri, Rayagada, Koraput and Kalahandi likely to be among the worst affected.
At least 46,701 people have been evacuated so far, while 448 cyclone shelters have been made operational and another 3,000 are being readied, the officials cited above said. Pregnant women, elderly people and children have been prioritised for evacuation, while residents in hilly areas have been asked to move to safer locations in view of the possibility of landslides.
As many as 60 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams and 14 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams have been deployed for rescue and relief operations.
The chief minister has directed officials to accord the highest priority to ensuring zero casualties and asked ministers and MLAs to coordinate preparedness measures in potentially affected areas. The government has also provided ₹1 crore each as advance assistance to Ganjam and other districts that are likely to be impacted.
Schools and anganwadi centres in nine districts will remain closed on Thursday and Friday in view of the cyclone threat. The State Selection Board (SSB) has also postponed its scheduled recruitment examinations due to the forecast of heavy rainfall over the next two days.
Four senior officials of the Water Resources department have been assigned to monitor river levels and flood risks in different districts from Friday to Sunday and coordinate precautionary measures with the Engineer-in-Chief.

The Congress on Wednesday formed a 42-member election committee for poll-bound Punjab that included party veteran Ambika Soni and Chandigarh MP Manish Tewari after he was earlier ignored for other election-related panels, people familiar with the matter said.

The party also included former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and former Punjab unit chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring—bringing the two leaders of the contending factions together, they said.

The inclusion of Tewari assumes importance as he was left out of all other poll-related panels on the ground that he is a lawmaker from Chandigarh. Tewari had been a former MP from Punjab and won Anandpur Sahib in the 2019 election.
Partap Singh Bajwa, the Congress Legislative Party (CLP) leader in the Punjab assembly, former CM Rajinder Kaur Bhattal, Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, another powerful Jatt Sikh leader, former MP Vijay Inder Singla who is arguably the most famous Hindu face of the party and Shamsher Singh Dullo— a prominent Ramdasia Sikh.
In an important move, the party also included Amethi MP Kishori Lal Sharma, who was born in Hoshiarpur but later shifted to Uttar Pradesh, in the committee, the people said.
The committee, approved by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, includes several prominent state and national leaders but didn’t include Navjyot Singh Siddhu, the former Punjab PCC chief who was a prominent feature in the similar list for the 2021 election.
AICC general secretary in-charge of Punjab Sachin Pilot, the secretaries and heads of all frontal organisations have been included in the team.

morning.text:
Ombudspersons must attend at least 3 gram sabhas a month
District-level ombudspersons under the new rural employment law will be required to attend at least three social audit public hearings, or gram sabhas, every month to hear people’s grievances, according to guidelines the ministry of rural development issued on Wednesday
District-level ombudspersons under the new rural employment law will be required to attend at least three social audit public hearings, or gram sabhas, every month to hear people’s grievances, according to guidelines the ministry of rural development issued on Wednesday. The guidelines also provide for a digital platform to track complaints, record proceedings and monitor action taken.
The government issued the new Guidelines for Ombudsperson and Appellate Authority under the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), or VB-G RAM G, Act, 2025, which replaced the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).
To be sure, the district-level ombudsperson is not a new provision as MGNREGA also mandated states to appoint one in every district to receive complaints, conduct enquiries and pass awards.
While under earlier guidelines, issued in 2017, ombudspersons were also expected to be present at social audit public hearings, the latest guidelines specify a minimum of three such meetings every month.
The ministry described the ombudsperson as an “important link” in the programme’s accountability framework, providing rural citizens with an “accessible mechanism to raise complaints and seek appropriate redressal”.
The guidelines also provide for a dedicated digital platform for registering and tracking complaints, recording proceedings, uploading awards and monitoring action taken. Field visits will have to be documented through geo-tagged and time-stamped photographs.
Digital monitoring of complaints, too, is not entirely new as the ministry had launched an Ombudsperson App in February 2022 under MGNREGA to help record and categorise complaints. The new guidelines expand the pool of eligible candidates for appointment to include people with experience in rural development, public administration, law, academics, social work and management. The ministry has also revised provisions relating to tenure and remuneration.
The ombudsperson will handle complaints relating to job cards, denial of employment, wage payments, compensation for delayed wages, worksite facilities, muster rolls and denial of statutory entitlements. The guidelines also cover discrimination, harassment and violations of the rights of women and vulnerable groups.
“The guidelines emphasise field visits, community engagement and familiarity with digital platforms. Social audit findings and community feedback, along with individual grievances, will support the identification of discrepancies and corrective action in accordance with prescribed procedures,” the ministry said.
The guidelines come weeks after the ministry notified separate Grievance Redressal Rules under the VB-G RAM G programme on November 2. The rules mandate complaints to be examined within seven working days and resolved within 15 days, with unresolved complaints escalated to the next level.

morning.title: India imposes 162.5% tax on bulk Scotch imports amid UK trade pact standoff
morning.text:
India imposes 162.5% tax on bulk Scotch imports amid UK trade pact standoff
The India-UK trade agreement implemented in July halved tariff rates on Scotch to 75%.
Amid a raging dispute over the India-UK trade pact, India is now imposing an effective duty of 162.5% on bulk Scotch imports, jolting liquor firms as the levies exceed the 150% charged before the landmark agreement, according to eight sources and a government document.
The India-UK trade agreement implemented in July halved tariff rates on Scotch to 75%, and businesses and Britain both hailed it as a big win for companies like Pernod Ricard and Diageo, which import Scotch in bulk and blend it to make popular products for India's $65 billion liquor market.
But in the first major dispute linked to the India-UK pact, Indian investigators have argued companies are using wrong customs classifications in importing bulk Scotch concentrates - these are deemed to be raw material used to make drinks like blended whiskies.
Also Read: Making the India-EU trade deal work for Tiruppur and Moradabad
Since May, such imports, Indian investigators argue, come under a newly created customs line for so-called “compound alcoholic preparations", which attracts a 150% tariff.
These imports then attract a consumption tax which takes the full duty amount to 162.5%, according to a government document reviewed by Reuters and eight sources, including industry executives and customs agents, who have direct knowledge of the matter.
As the standoff drags on, thousands of litres of bulk Scotch in more than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod, Diageo and Bacardi have been stuck at ports, Reuters reported last week.
Under a so-called provisional release pending investigation, duty at 75% of the goods’ value needs to be paid up front, with the rest covered by bank guarantees, the sources said.
"Industry has already reduced prices of Scotch products in the market when the India-UK pact kicked in, and now they are faced with higher duties again," said a source in the liquor importing business.
Pernod, which owns UK-based Chivas Brothers, Diageo and many other Indian companies believe Scotch imports - bulk and bottled both - should be taxed only at 75% as per the trade pact.
The British government has repeatedly said in statements it is working with New Delhi on the issue, while India has said the dispute will be resolved soon.
Pernod and Diageo have moved to arrange bank guarantees and other funding to get their blocked containers released so that business can continue, while Bacardi is still deciding its next steps, said three of the sources.
Diageo declined to comment, while Pernod and Bacardi did not respond to queries. The Indian finance ministry and the tax authority also did not respond.
Businesses fear disruptions
Long-drawn tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors and have hit the likes of Volkswagen and Samsung. Indian officials say they only enforce the law of the land, but executives say they are often caught off guard by how New Delhi classifies imports.
Mumbai-listed majors Radico Khaitan, Allied Blenders and Distillers and Tilaknagar Industries all import bulk Scotch and are under scrutiny, like Pernod and Diageo. Smaller companies can face more stress in arranging bank guarantees as they may require collateral. Such guarantees also need to be reported as contingent liabilities.

The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has asked its affiliated schools to enrol at least three to five experienced teachers as mentors under the Centre’s Mentoring Initiative for Teaching, Research and Assessment (MITRA), aimed at strengthening professional development and capacity building among school teachers.
In a circular dated November 16, addressed to principals and heads of all 33,287 CBSE-affiliated schools, the board said the initiative, launched by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) under the Union education ministry, seeks to build a national pool of experienced professionals who can mentor teachers across the country.
The initiative, envisaged under National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, aims to provide “personalised mentoring support to in-service teachers, enabling them to become reflective practitioners and lifelong learners,” the board said.
The CBSE has asked school heads to disseminate the information and facilitate the enrolment of eligible teachers on the National Mission for Mentoring (NMM) portal of NCTE.
Also Read: CBSE Class 10, 12 board exams to be conducted from February 16, board issues datesheet
Focus areas
According to the circular, applicants must have a minimum of eight years of professional experience, demonstrated expertise in one or more identified mentoring domains, effective communication and digital skills, and a willingness to contribute to the mission.
The mentoring framework covers 45 domains and sub-domains spanning teaching practices, educational policies, classroom management, child development, inclusive education, mental health and wellness, assessment, leadership, and professional development. It also includes specialised areas such as artificial intelligence in education, cybersecurity, and subject-specific pedagogy in mathematics, science, social sciences, languages and other disciplines.
The NCTE will organise online orientation sessions every Tuesday from 3:30pm to 4:30pm to familiarise prospective mentors with the portal, registration and onboarding process, and the conduct of mentoring sessions. The sessions will also address queries from applicants.
Kiran Bedi joins national mentor pool

From NMM to MITRA
The National Mission for Mentoring (NMM) was pilot-launched on July 29, 2022, across 30 central schools. The initiative was renamed MITRA on August 17, 2026, on the NCTE’s 32nd Foundation Day.

The MITRA Bluebook, a guiding document for the initiative, was launched by the education ministry in August 2026. The framework envisages a mentor-mentee ratio of 1:5, with experienced professionals providing short- and long-term support to teachers through structured interactions.
The mission seeks to strengthen continuous professional development and encourage cross-learning among school teachers.

morning.text:
SC seeks responses from parties on traders’ plea against Ramlila Maidan as protest venue
The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought responses from political parties, including the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and organisations such as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and the All India Students Union (AISA), on a petition by market traders’ associations challenging the designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue
The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought responses from political parties, including the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and organisations such as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and the All India Students Union (AISA), on a petition by market traders’ associations challenging the designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue. The traders have argued that demonstrations at the ground disrupt business, affect livelihoods and deny access to roads leading to nearby residential areas.
A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant issued notices on a petition filed by the Kirana Committee of Delhi and the Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchants Association of Chawri Bazar on October 16, ahead of a proposed “Lehra Do Tiranga” march organised by the CJP at Connaught Place, with participation by AISA, on the same day.
The bench, also comprising justices Joymalya and V Mohana, sought responses from the Centre, the Delhi government, the Congress, the AAP, the CJP and AISA. It agreed to take up the matter after two weeks.
Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for the petitioners, said, “I am also challenging the notification of Ramlila Maidan as a protest site is also wrong. This location is within close proximity of prominent markets such as Connaught Place, Chandni Chowk, Chawri Bazar, Khari Baoli and Sadar Bazar.”
Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, told the top court that the matter has to be taken up with the petitions challenging the police action during the Delhi protests. Mehta said, “This court is hearing the other set of petitions seeking their right to protest. And this matter is protesting that right citing the fundamental rights of traders, workers, and residents. These are contesting rights and should be heard together.”
In their petition, the traders said Ramlila Maidan was “surrounded by dense residential localities and wholesale and retail markets of Old Delhi, where thousands of workers, traders and vendors operate”. They argued that the designation was made without a published assessment of its impact on residents and businesses, or safeguards concerning the number of demonstrators, duration of protests, damage to property and liability.
On November 3, while hearing the petition, the court had asked whether the organisations that had called for protests had been made parties to the case. Following the suggestion, the petitioners added the Congress, which organised a rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, along with the AAP, the CJP and AISA.
The bench had observed that protests affected the livelihood of people working in shops and those earning their living by selling goods on carts and stalls.
The traders had initially approached the court over an order issued by the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) to close Central Park in Connaught Place for the proposed march. The subsequent rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, they said, reinforced their concerns about the suitability of the ground as a protest venue.
The petition seeks quashing of the October 11 order issued by Delhi Police designating Ramlila Maidan as a protest site, and a fresh, reasoned assessment after considering the surrounding areas and the interests of those affected.
The Kirana Committee said the protests had come during the weeks when traders earned a substantial share of their annual income. “In the very weeks on which its traders earn their year, due to illegal and unlawful protests conducted in the midst of festive season, the livelihood of the vendors has suffered a significant loss,” the petition said.
It estimated that Delhi sees daily business of around ₹500 crore to ₹600 crore, of which about ₹250 crore was at risk each day during the peak season between October 2026 and January 2027. The petition said nearly one million establishments, 10 million livelihoods and around 500,000 outstation traders depended on this activity.
The petitioners said the impact extended beyond business owners to employees, daily-wage workers, street vendors, hawkers, delivery personnel, drivers and artisans.
They clarified that they were not seeking a ban on peaceful protests, but wanted a framework governing the location, duration and scale of demonstrations, traffic arrangements and continued access to markets, residential neighbourhoods, hospitals and public transport. They also sought preventive planning and enforcement of the law in cases of violence or vandalism, while clarifying that such conduct should not be attributed to peaceful demonstrators generally.

morning.title: DGCA proposes separate registration system for prototype, production aircraft
morning.text:
DGCA proposes separate registration system for prototype, production aircraft
Under the proposed framework, a common pool of registration marks will be created for production and prototype aircraft
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has proposed a separate registration mechanism for aircraft undergoing production and prototype testing, allowing manufacturers to obtain dedicated registration marks for test flights without entering the aircraft in India’s regular civil aircraft register.
The proposal is part of a revised set of Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) governing aircraft registration and de-registration, which also seeks to tighten documentation requirements for aircraft taken on dry lease and prevent the reallocation of registration marks once an aircraft has been entered in the Indian Civil Aircraft Register.
Applying for dedicated registration marks
Under the proposed framework, a common pool of registration marks will be created for production and prototype aircraft. Applicants will be required to apply through the DGCA’s e-GCA portal using a separate application form and submit production approval documents. These could include a letter of agreement issued by the Aircraft Engineering Directorate or production organisation approval issued by the DGCA or a foreign civil aviation authority.
Also Read: US FAA begins 5-day audit of DGCA’s safety oversight system
The registration fee will be calculated on the basis of the aircraft’s maximum take-off weight (MTOW), as specified in its type certificate data sheet or the letter of agreement issued by the Aircraft Engineering Directorate.
The registration marks will be allocated exclusively for production and prototype test flights. Such aircraft will not be entered in the Indian Civil Aircraft Register in the same manner as aircraft in service and cannot be used for any other purpose under this registration.
The draft also specifies that the certificate of registration issued for these aircraft will expire once the manufacturer issues a statement of design conformity (Form CA-52) or an equivalent document. The certificate holder will then have to obtain a certificate of non-registration from the DGCA before the registration mark can be reused for another production or prototype aircraft. The expired registration mark and the aircraft’s 24-bit address, or Mode-S code, will also have to be removed.
Proposed changes to dry-lease applications and registration marks
Separately, the DGCA has proposed that applications for registration of aircraft taken on dry lease must be accompanied by a copy of the lease agreement and an original ‘no binding certificate’ from the owner, lessor, lessee and mortgagee, as applicable. The certificate must state that no clause of the lease agreement is binding on the regulator.
Another proposed change states that once an aircraft is entered in the Indian Civil Aircraft Register, its registration mark cannot be reallocated.
Also Read: Hold the line on pilot rest
Changes amid efforts to strengthen aircraft leasing
The proposed revision comes against the backdrop of the government’s efforts to strengthen the country’s aircraft leasing and financing ecosystem.
Parliament passed the Protection of Interest in Aircraft Objects Bill, 2025, in April last year, to align India’s framework with the Cape Town Convention, an international agreement governing interests in high-value mobile assets, including aircraft.
Also Read: More teeth for the aviation regulator
India acceded to the convention in 2008, but gaps in its legal enforcement framework had resulted in aircraft leasing costs being 8-10% higher than in other countries, according to the civil aviation ministry. The legislation seeks to provide greater legal certainty to aircraft financiers, make India a more attractive destination for aircraft leasing and help reduce costs for domestic carriers.
The DGCA has invited comments on the proposed revision before finalising the changes.

morning.text:
Indian economy in dire straits, Rahul Gandhi says in US; BJP hits out
Speaking at Columbia University, Rahul Gandhi said India faces severe unemployment and education challenges.
India is sitting on an economic disaster with massive unemployment and a poor education system, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said on Wednesday, triggering criticism from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Addressing a gathering at Columbia University in New York, the Congress MP also blamed the Union government, reiterated his allegations of vote theft and said street protests in India were a reflection of young people’s socioeconomic frustration.
“The blunt thing is: India is sitting on an economic disaster. That’s the reality. And one can brush it aside. The media can brush it aside. But India’s got a massive unemployment problem. India has got a massive problem with its education system,” Gandhi told his audience, arguing that the central government’s signature initiatives such as Make in India and Startup India had failed to make a difference.
Also read: India calls for equitable, country-driven approach to global just transition at COP31
Gandhi questions impact of Make in India, Startup India
In a speech substantially focused on economics and geopolitics, Gandhi compared India’s economic model to that of China, noting that the latter had made great strides in building manufacturing and providing blue-collar jobs.
“I’m interested from an Indian perspective in production in a democratic environment. It’s not that India has not done this. India used to do this and has had success in this. But you cannot have two businessmen controlling the entire architecture of a country and expect manufacturing,” he said.
“That economic model stopped giving results almost a decade ago. The Prime Minister has been putting out one idea after another. Make in India, Startup India, all of these things..But what has happened? Absolutely nothing. Because the spine of the economy has been broken,” Gandhi said, taking aim at the Modi government’s flagship economic policies.
Also read: Rahul Gandhi posts ‘Satyam Shivam Sundaram’ after BJP dig; Himanta Sarma hits back
Gandhi links global protests to economic uncertainty
In the 90-minute interaction, Gandhi also dwelled on America’s political and economic problems, given the fundamental challenge China poses to Washington’s previously unrivalled claims to superpower status. He linked this churn to protests around the world.
“Why is it happening in one way in the United States? Why is it happening in Brazil? Why is it happening in so many different places? So it can’t be that all these countries are coming to the same conclusion at the same time. So, to me, you can’t separate what is happening in India or what is happening in France with what is happening on the planet, with what is happening to the larger economic substrate. To me, a lot of this is connected,” Gandhi said.
He noted that India’s lower costs and larger population made it relatively easier for the country to provide jobs for its youth, compared with countries such as the US or Germany.
“Our costs are lower and we have bigger numbers. Indians can take a lot more suffering and pain. It’s a fact. Maybe I shouldn’t be saying this,” Gandhi said of India’s future economic prospects.

Rahul Gandhi reiterates allegations of electoral malpractice
Gandhi reiterated allegations about electoral malpractice and reiterated his party’s determination to remove chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar from office.
“The idea is to restore the electoral system. Without that, nothing is going to happen, and we are working on that. We have a lot of proof on electoral malpractice. There are many people now in the system who are very scared, who are now speaking to us. I see it in quite a positive light,” he said, while adding that he feared the Indian government would react “violently and aggressively” in the face of growing public pressure.
Gandhi’s remarks at Columbia University marked the first of his two planned public engagements in the US. He will speak at the University of Chicago on Thursday.

The BJP hit back. “Whenever Rahul Gandhi travels abroad, he makes false statements. His sole intention is to undermine India’s progress and weaken the strong international image that the country is building,” party spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said.
Bhatia alleged that Gandhi’s remarks were intended to damage India’s international standing at a time when the country was making progress on several fronts.
“Why should the citizens of India feel ashamed because of the statements of a Leader of the Opposition who makes such remarks against the country?” he said.

Azam Khan out of jail; Supreme Court refuses to stay in interim bail in ED case
The ED had challenged the Allahabad High Court's interim bail order, questioning its findings on the circumstances surrounding Khan's arrest on October 31.
Senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan walked out of Ghaziabad’s Dasna jail in Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday, hours after the Supreme Court refused to stay his release on interim bail in a money laundering case. However, the court agreed to hear the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED’s) challenge to the Allahabad High Court order granting him relief.
The release warrant reached Dasna jail at around 4.30 pm, following which formalities were completed and Khan was allowed to walk out. He left for his hometown Rampur.
Akhilesh Yadav calls release a victory of truth
Deep Dive
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav described his release as a victory of truth and expressed confidence that Khan would continue to get justice. “Truth has triumphed. We have complete faith in the judiciary. He will get justice even in the future,” Akhilesh Yadav said in Gorakhpur.
Earlier in the day, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant declined an urgent hearing sought by additional solicitor general SV Raju, appearing for ED, on Wednesday itself and asked the agency to argue its objections before the court on Thursday.
Seeking an immediate hearing, Raju questioned the high court’s findings, contending that it had granted bail as though it had already concluded the trial and had characterised the investigation as “malafide”. He also objected to the high court’s observation that Khan’s arrest was motivated, pointing out that ED had arrested him soon after he walked out of jail in another case. “No. Not today. You argue all these points before the court concerned tomorrow,” CJI Kant told the law officer, making clear that the matter would be listed on Thursday.
When Raju sought a direction to maintain status quo until then, expressing apprehension that Khan could be released in the meantime, justice Joymalya Bagchi, sitting on the bench led by the CJI, declined to intervene.
“Let him be on interim bail. Heavens will not fall,” the judge remarked.

Allahabad HC cited alleged lapses in arrest procedure
The Allahabad High Court granted Khan interim bail on Tuesday, prima facie finding that ED had not strictly followed the mandatory safeguards governing arrest under Article 22(1) of the Constitution and Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).
The high court, comprising justices Rajiv Gupta and Devendra Singh, had questioned the circumstances in which the 78-year-old leader was arrested on October 31, minutes after he was released from Rampur district jail following bail in a separate forgery case. It described the timing of the arrest as indicative of a “motivated and mala fide” exercise.
The case relates to alleged financial irregularities involving the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, founded and controlled by Khan.

morning.title: Bigger than any movie, ever: Grand Theft Auto VI arrives in record-shattering media release
morning.text:
Bigger than any movie, ever: Grand Theft Auto VI arrives in record-shattering media release
GTA VI — releasing 13 long years since the previous iteration — is the sequel to a game that sold more than 220 million copies.
The world has just witnessed the biggest entertainment release in history — and it isn’t a Hollywood movie. Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI began rolling out for users on Wednesday evening, as the global release of the long-awaited video game capped a protracted eight-year development saga.
But even before consoles around the world began booting GTA VI — the game was released for Indian users at midnight on Thursday — it had made more money than any film has ever earned in its opening weekend. Rockstar Games’s follow-up to GTA V had booked about $1.5 billion — roughly ₹14,100 crore — in pre-orders by Wednesday, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. Avengers: Endgame, which holds the record for the biggest global opening in cinema history, made $1.2 billion in its first weekend in 2019.
As reviews began trickling in, GTA VI debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator Metacritic, combining the numbers of 145 reviews. Gaming news website IGN called it “the single most impressive video game ever”. The Verge said: “Grand Theft Auto VI does something impossible – it lives up to the hype.”
Deep Dive
For nearly three decades, Grand Theft Auto has sold players a world of sex, drugs and rock ’n’ roll, with fast cars and crime money, inviting praise and criticism in equal measure. And few pieces of pop culture have carried this much weight. GTA VI — releasing 13 long years since the previous iteration — is the sequel to a game that sold more than 220 million copies and defined a generation of gaming.
Also Read: GTA 6 first reviews out: New Zealand gamers praise 'insane' graphics, say game 'did not disappoint'
The stock of Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent company, surged as high as 7.70% as GTA VI officially began its regional unlock, with New Zealand going live first as the clock struck midnight (4.30pm IST). By multiple industry estimates, GTA VI could generate $3 billion and sell 30 million copies by the end of the year.
India also had a special appearance as media entertainment history was created.
The Rockstar India studio in Bengaluru built partly after the 2019 acquisition of Dhruva Interactive, often called the country’s oldest game developer, is part of Rockstar’s global network. While Rockstar has not said if the Bengaluru operations contributed to GTA VI, when the studio’s previous big game — Red Dead Redemption 2 — came out, the India team was all over the post-game credits.
GTA VI has also cost more money to make than any film in history. Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have yet to disclose the budget, but industry analysts cited by Yahoo Finance put the most credible range at $1-2 billion, or about ₹9,400-18,800 crore.
Even the lower end of that range puts it beyond Hollywood. The most expensive films ever made are reported to have cost around $500-600 million. Back home, the recently released Ramayana, billed as India’s costliest film, is said to have a budget of ₹4,000 crore for its two parts combined, which is a little under $500 million.
Take-Two chief executive Strauss Zelnick has called GTA VI “arguably the most anticipated entertainment property of all time”.
The series has long been at the receiving end of praise, ridicule and even pure hate. Its satire of glamour, crime, American excess and celebrity culture has drawn both appreciation and concerns over violence. The sixth edition of the game follows Lucia and Jason, a criminal couple, through an influencer-age parody of Florida. GTA VI also signals a studio that has changed with its audience. Lucia is the first female lead of the series in its modern era. Bloomberg reported in 2022 that Rockstar was reining in jokes aimed at marginalised groups as part of an overhaul of its workplace culture.
Rockstar has called Leonida, its fantasy-world take on Florida, “the biggest, most immersive evolution of the Grand Theft Auto series yet”.
The game, however, is capped at 30 frames per second on every console, even the PS5 Pro, leading to initial complaints of sluggishness in some scenes.
Rockstar first revealed the game in December 2023 with a promise of a 2025 release. The deadline then slipped twice: first to May 26, 2026, and then to November 19. “These extra months will allow us to finish the game with the level of polish you have come to expect and deserve,” the gaming studio said at the time. One of the trailers, released in May 2025, drew 475 million views in 24 hours.
The main part of the game is estimated to take around 50 hours to complete, so full reactions will not be available immediately.
But some fans have said they will stay up all night and/or take the day off work to dive straight in.
“(When) ‘Grand Theft Auto V’ came out I was a child, and so the anticipation is crazy,” Brayden Whaley, a 23-year-old content creator from Los Angeles told news agency Reuters.

morning.title: Chinese web giant Tencent says new US GPU ban ‘sets everyone back in China’
morning.text:
The USA’s new ban on Chinese companies remotely accessing GPUs will have short-term impact, but ultimately see China accelerate its development of domestic alternatives, according to Martin Lau, the president of Chinese web giant Tencent.

Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Lau said the new US regulation will have an “unfortunate” impact on Tencent’s business.

“It does set everyone back. It sets everyone back in China,” Lau said. “So everyone is actually having less advanced compute to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China.”

He said the ban will impact Tencent’s ability to train models.

“Our training efficiency with Hy4 is actually very high,” he said. “When we look at the next version, it would take probably longer time for us to come up with the next version in the short run.”

“But over time, the domestic supply chain would actually come on board.”

Lau also thinks the bans won’t hamper Tencent’s ability to run inferencing workloads, because made-in-China chips “should be able to cover it.”

“And over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we see the industry is progressing very fast,” he added. “With the latest restriction, we expect it to actually speed up even further, because all the development effort would actually have to be focused on speeding up the domestic supply chain.”

Tencent needs GPUs, and lots of them, because the 10 million users of its agentic assistant WorkBuddy are collectively consuming over 100 trillion tokens per day. Lau thinks WorkBuddy is on track to becoming a hit product, partly because many users are outside China.

Lau said Tencent can serve WorkBuddy customers outside China because the service can operate with different models, and the company thinks it can find third parties to provide the necessary inferencing services without the new US bans creating a problem.

But Lau said that GPU rentals and other cloud services, which are also growing strongly, may be impacted.

“In terms of cloud, if it is non-GPU related, we can actually build capacities ourselves outside of China,” he said. “I think there is still a lot of such opportunities because our cloud service is actually very cost competitive. When it comes to GPU, then unfortunately, we cannot actually offer high-end GPU anymore. We may be able to work with some partners in different places.”

Tencent doesn’t break out revenue for its cloud services, but said they rose by 35 percent year-on-year, well ahead of the company’s overall eight percent growth. Marketing services also grew strongly, by 19 percent, thanks in part to new AI-powered systems that improve ad targeting.

The company’s WeChat and Weixin messaging platforms continued to grow, adding 35 million accounts to exiting the quarter with 1.44 billion monthly active users.

One Tencent biz that went backwards was its international gaming unit, which saw revenue fall nine percent.

Chief strategy officer James Mitchell said that slowdown wasn’t caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. “I think that in fairness, the slowdown for us predated the run-up to GTA VI,” he said, before predicting that Tencent’s existing and future “evergreen games” should help to turn things around.

GPUs might help, too.

“The game environment globally is one where the rate of innovation has slowed somewhat, and now with AI, there’s opportunities to re-accelerate innovation,” he said. ®

morning.text: Mumbai: An eclectic mix of niche consumer businesses-from luxury catering and commercial gym equipment makers to baby- and adult-hygiene products and B2B hospitality providers-would seek to collectively raise about ₹10,000-12,000 crore through initial public offerings (IPOs) in December, rounding off a likely record year of share sales for India's primary markets.Foodlink F&B Holdings (luxury catering and banqueting), Jerai Fitness (commercial gym equipment), Swara Baby Products (disposable hygiene products), Nobel Hygiene (baby- and adult-hygiene products), Cult.fit (fitness and wellness) and PRISM, formerly OYO (global hospitality technology), are among the companies preparing for their market debut, bankers told ET.135974641Several of these companies operate in niche segments, with very few or no directly comparable listed players in India. "Investors now look for exposure to consumption themes that were earlier accessible only through private markets: premium experiences, fitness and wellness, and everyday hygiene," said Neha Agarwal, managing director and head of equity capital markets, JM Financial. The companies cited above have already received regulatory approvals for share sales and plan to launch their issues next month.Read more: Explained: Why did central banks just buy 320 tonnes of gold this quarter and can this last amid uncertainty?Rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and growing health awareness are creating large, under-penetrated categories, and these companies have built scale and brand recall in these segments.For promoters and private equity backers, deep domestic liquidity as well as strong participation from mutual funds and retail investors make this a good window to list, Agarwal said.Also, with financialisation, more varied companies are approaching the market, but each company is a clear market leader in its niche, whether from the standpoint of geography or business category, said Arka Mookerjee, partner at JSA.Read more: Largecaps pull ahead of small and mid caps in Q2 profit growth by over 25%. What’s driving the gap?"The regulatory landscape is also changing rapidly to track the feedback from each new issuance. A new ICDR (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) regulation is on the horizon and hopefully that will help get more of the next-100 companies on to the main boards," he said.Calendar year 2026, which saw the mega IPOs of Jio Platforms and the National Stock Exchange (NSE), is on course to end in a bumper haul for India's primary markets, which garnered Rs 1.58 lakh crore in IPOs until October despite a rather listless secondary market. The Sensex and the Nifty, which had underperformed until then, have since climbed more than 10% each on robust foreign fund flows.Among the companies preparing to list, Foodlink F&B Holdings has planned an IPO with a fresh issue of Rs 160 crore and offer for sale (OFS) of 12 million shares. The company is promoted by Sanjay Vazirani and operates across luxury catering, banqueting, casual dining restaurants and cloud kitchens.It has operations in India, the UAE, the UK and Malaysia.The proposed IPO by Jerai Fitness will entirely be an OFS of 4.39 million shares. The company manufactures strength and cardiovascular equipment for gyms, hotels, clubs, residential and commercial projects, and educational institutions.Its products are sold under the Jerai Fitness and Reebok brands.The IPO of Swara Baby Products, likely of Rs 1,000 crore, consists of a fresh issue and an OFS. The company manufactures disposable hygiene products across baby care, adult incontinence and feminine hygiene categories.The Nobel Hygiene IPO will comprise a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and OFS of 15.5 million shares. It has built a presence across adult, baby and feminine absorbent hygiene categories.Its Friends brand pioneered the adult absorbent hygiene category in India.Cult.fit has planned an IPO of Rs 4,000 crore, consisting of a fresh issue and an OFS. morning.title: Get ready for another critical PHP security release to drop
morning.text:
Apologies in advance to all patch managers and security teams that thought they might get a break this week. The PHP Foundation will release a “critical” security update on Thursday between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC.

While we don’t have many details about the latest vulnerabilities – these haven’t been leaked like last month’s critical PHP2Shell flaws – a Wednesday advisory said the highest-severity bugs in the upcoming release are rated critical.

“The issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups,” the foundation said, urging PHP users to “prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available.”

We do know that one of the vulnerabilities is another remote code execution (RCE) flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-115560.

In October, the PHP Foundation told The Register that it had reserved this CVE identifier for another RCE bug, but added it would not get an emergency fix like the earlier two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities because the third one doesn't pose the same risk.

CVE-2026-115560 “requires a very unlikely combination of configuration and specific PHP application code, which we do not expect to occur in practical use of PHP,” Elizabeth Barron, executive director of the PHP Foundation, told The Register at the time. “The issue can be mitigated with a configuration setting. So for the moment the PHP Security Team has only published an informational advisory on the PHP website, explaining exactly this situation.”

The earlier informational advisory urged users to “set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.”

These unlikely RCE attacks require an application to set “session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start().”

Additionally, the session upload progress feature must be enabled, which the PHP Foundation said is very unlikely in real-world applications.

The November security release follows a hectic October emergency PHP patch-a-thon, with security teams racing to apply fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, before attackers could abuse the memory-safety flaws in the open source programming language running on about 70 percent of websites.

While it took miscreants longer to reverse engineer the PHP2Shell fixes than some researchers had anticipated – and the entire internet didn’t burn down in the meantime – the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) did add the two PHP vulns to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26.

Suspected Chinese attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls linked to US government-affiliated organizations, as early as October 23, according to Dream researchers.

The Israeli AI cybersecurity startup said the attackers targeted organizations across the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, and “likely still” have persistent, remote access to compromised organizations’ networks. ®

morning.title: AI found more critical bugs in another widely used technology running 225M websites
morning.text:
Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX.

These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services.

“At this time, we have found no evidence of active exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities in the wild,” and F5 spokesperson told The Register. “We continue to monitor closely and will share updates via myF5 as we learn more.”

As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years.

Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently.

Schwartz told The Register that this wave of AI-discovered flaws “point to a new reality.”

“We need to treat every internet-connected system as potentially vulnerable,” Schwartz said. “AI has changed not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.”

NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million), and F5 maintains the open source version.

On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible.

CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007

Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server.

All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5.

“Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic,” Schwartz and fellow Wiz kid Nir Ohfeld said in a Wednesday blog about the two bugs. “In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. In CVE-2026-123007, incorrect flow-control accounting leads to an invalid memory copy.”

Rapid7’s team also published a proof-of-concept to demonstrate leveraging CVE-2026-123007 for unauthenticated remote code execution against a vulnerable linux/amd64 Docker image running nginx version 1.31.8.

Xint found three other NGINX flaws, plus a separate vulnerability in the Linux kernel that can be chained with any of the five NGINX vulnerabilities to gain root privileges on the host. The research team dubbed the six bugs “nginx2root.”

The AI-powered offensive security firm also published videos demonstrating attacks using CVE-2026-123007 to execute commands as the NGINX worker inside a container, and then using the kernel vulnerability to escalate to root on the host. These attacks work on AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and bare-metal servers.

AI-powered bug hunting for the win?

"While preparing for ZeroDay Cloud 2026, a Xint researcher found CVE-2026-123007," the company said in a Wednesday blog. "A few days later, a fully automated Xint scan found the other four without human guidance."

All of these newly-disclosed CVEs point to a larger security issue - especially in light of Tuesday’s Java4Shell, found by AI-bug-hunting-outfit Calif, PHP2Shell (Calif was one of the firms that also used AI to find and weaponize these critical vulns in PHP), and a critical Apache flaw under active exploitation .

“AI is also accelerating vulnerability discovery faster than existing infrastructure was designed to absorb,” Schwartz told us. “Even after a vendor ships a fix, security teams still face heavy manual work in terms of locating vulnerable versions and configurations, testing patches, deploying interim mitigations (such as disabling HTTP/2), and coordinating all of these rollouts.”

There is light at the end of the tunnel, he believes. “In the long run, AI-powered vulnerability research will harden foundational software.”

But in the meantime, it’s a nightmare for security teams, vulnerability managers, and system administrators, who are drowning in the near-daily deluge of CVEs to patch before attackers find and exploit these vulnerabilities.

“Continued collaboration between security researchers, maintainers, and defenders is crucial to absorb the speed and scale of these disclosures,” Schwartz said.®
