morning.title: To rank the world's biggest supercomputers, we're gonna need a bigger bench
morning.text:
For decades, the Top500 list has tirelessly ranked the world’s biggest, most powerful, and often most unique publicly-known supercomputers.

With the rise of generative AI, the list no longer lives up to its name. China’s Lineshine supercomputer at 2.2 exaFLOPS of double precision compute in the High-Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark may be the top system on the bi-annual ranking, but it’s nowhere near the biggest compute cluster in the world.

Superclusters like SpaceXAI’s Colossus, Meta’s Promethius, and OpenAI’s Stargate pack hundreds of thousands of GPUs, dwarfing anything on the Top500 today.

“These [companies] are not interested in submitting to the Top500,” Eth Zürich’s Torsten Hoefler said during his Supercomputing address this week.

It’s a dilemma that the founders of the Top500 ranking are now grappling with. And some believe it may be time for a rethink.

“What’s really needed for tracking that more appropriately is not just a different benchmark but also different methodology,” Top500 author Erich Strohmaier said.

For a long time, Strohmaier explains, compute capability was roughly aligned with capacity.

What happened in the last few years with AI is “capacity really pulled ahead of capability in terms of market size,” he said. “We were and we still are very focused on capability.”

By capability, Strohmaier is referring to the ability to run one code across the entire cluster.

“Our prime rule for benchmarking is, you have to benchmark your whole system with one code and you cannot just add two parts up to make up a number,” he explained.

This is problematic for the large clusters major hyperscalers and cloud providers are now building to fuel the AI boom. “All those systems are capacity systems,” Strohmaier said.

They’re not designed to run one piece of code but have instead been architected to run many, many smaller or medium-sized code instantiations, which may include training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and of course inference.

Because of this, Strohmaier says, it wouldn’t be reasonable to expect SpaceXAI to run something High-Performance Linpack (HPL) on a cluster like Colossus.

But these clusters are still worth tracking. They'll just need a new benchmark better suited to judging the capability of these arrays while at the same time preventing operators from gaming the system.

What shape or form such a benchmark might take remains to be seen. Developing a new benchmark or methodology is no small task, and changing the existing benchmarks isn’t ideal. ”If we do anything to the benchmark itself, we’re going to lose the historic trends, which is extremely valuable,” Hoefler said.

Allowing for lower precisions — HPL-MxP already does this to some extent — is one avenue for addressing the fact that these accelerators are increasingly trading FP64 performance for lower-accuracy floating-point data types like FP8 or FP4.

Another avenue is developing a separate AI benchmark. This would be immediately applicable to these clusters, but with the pace of change in model architecture, building such a benchmark is challenging.

“The AI workloads change every two weeks, so if you pick something today, it’s going to be irrelevant in at most a year, and these benchmarks need to live for multiple decades,” Hoefler said. ®

The Supreme Court will hear on Friday a petition seeking action against an Italian political functionary for raising a “demeaning political slogan” at Bharat Summit 2026 in Telangana and an apology by the Telangana government, which organised the event.
The petition, filed by a lawyer Zahid Ali, was mentioned on Wednesday by advocate Syed Rizvan Ahmad for urgent hearing claiming that the objectionable comments were made by Giacomo Filibeck, an Italian political representative and Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists, which amounts to interference with our democratic system.

Filibeck, while participating at the event organised on 13-14 November by the Telangana government, had said, “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod” – the political slogan coined by the Congress.
Immigration, visa, regulatory framework
Ahmad told the court that statements of foreign political representatives on Indian soil must adhere to the applicable immigration, visa and regulatory framework and strict action must be taken against any violation of the same.
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said, “We can list it on Friday. Rest you can argue before that bench.”
Ahmad told the court that the social media platforms must take down the post as such a comment by a foreign functionary on Indian soil is unacceptable. He said, “In my soil, he says we are convinced that the government is corrupted here and tells the Opposition to restore democracy.”

morning.title: PM Modi sets target for drug abuse eradication at ministers’ meet
morning.text:
PM Modi sets target for drug abuse eradication at ministers’ meet
A presentation at the meeting highlighted a World Bank report that found extreme poverty in India fell by 90% between 2011 and 2023.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday chaired a meeting of the council of ministers and underscored the need for a concerted campaign to eradicate drug use, said people aware of the details.
According to a person privy to the meeting, the PM expressed concern over the widespread social evil and said drug addiction had emerged as a major challenge for the country. He said just as the government took stern measures against left-wing terrorism and managed to pull out millions from poverty, there was a need to act against drug abuse, this person added.
“The prime minister was overcome with emotions when he spoke about the impact drugs use has on the younger demographic and said the social evil needs to be eradicated and no effort must be spared to do so...” said the person quoted above.
The Union government sharpens anti-drug campaign ahead of Punjab elections
The Union government has sharpened its campaign against drug abuse, particularly in poll-bound Punjab. In recent weeks, anti-drug campaigns have been the focus of Bharatiya Janata Party leaders including Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced that the party would fight the upcoming assembly elections in the northern state on the plank of “Nasha Mukt Punjab”(drug-free Punjab). On November 9, Shah at an event in Gujarat said that the Modi government now aims at creating a ‘Drug-free India’ by December 31, 2029.
At the three-hour meeting held at Bharat Mandapam in the Capital, two presentations on poverty alleviation and LWE eradication and cyber security were also made. The poverty alleviation presentation was made by Anuradha Thakur, secretary, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) and LWE eradication was discussed by Govind Mohan, Union home secretary.
“The presentation on poverty alleviation measures highlighted how 500 million people have been pulled out of poverty and the economic progress made over the past 12 years,” said the person quoted above.
The PM is learnt to have said that when the government was formed in 2014, he had referred to it as the government for the poor. He urged his colleagues to ensure that poverty alleviation measures were implemented well so that more people could have a quality life with access to health and education.
Also read: Target 2029: How big is India’s drug challenge? What the latest numbers tell us
Modi calls for continued vigilance against Maoism
Regarding the government’s achievements in curbing left-wing extremism, the PM cautioned that the government and law enforcement agencies must maintain their vigil to ensure that Maoism did not make a comeback.
“The government set itself a target to eradicate Naxalism and has been successful in doing so. The PM said both achievements, of alleviating poverty and curbing LWE, need to be celebrated,” said the person quoted above.
The ministers also discussed a World Bank poverty report stating that 500 million people were lifted out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, reducing the extreme poverty rate by 90%—from more than one in four Indians to roughly one in 38.
Also read: Two-day anti-narcotics conference: Inside India’s plan to go drug-free by 2047
The discussions also centered on governance reforms, employment generation, 100% saturation of welfare schemes, and targeted outreach toward youth and women—demographics heavily tied to India’s innovation and entrepreneurship push.

The money is likely to be kept in a dedicated redemption reserve account and paid on the due date, said the people cited above.Renegotiating Terms With TotalThe original plan had been to prepay the bond after special Reserve Bank of India (RBI) approval but the company decided against this move.“We do not comment on routine business matters. All public disclosures on business matters are disclosed when appropriate,” an Adani Group spokesperson told ET.Adani Green is also renegotiating the terms of its agreement with French utilities giant TotalEnergies for a proposed $4 billion investment in a green hydrogen venture, having signed a memorandum of understanding in 2022. In February, Total said it was pausing the plan in the wake of the Hindenburg Research report on the Adani Group alleging stock manipulation and fraud. The Adani Group has rejected the report’s findings.Total had said it won’t immediately proceed with the plan that involved taking a 25% stake in Adani New Industries Ltd (ANIL), a subsidiary of Adani Enterprises.In June last year, ANIL and TotalEnergies had outlined a capex plan of $50 billion to set up a 2.5 million metric tonnes per annum (mmtpa) of green hydrogen manufacturing capacity over the next 10 years, with the first phase of 1 mmtpa expected to be commissioned before 2030. Total had also made a total $10 billion capital commitment to the hydrogen venture, standing guarantor to 50% of the project’s debt, translating to $6 billion, ET had reported February 13.ANIL plans to manufacture green hydrogen and downstream products such as ammonia, urea, methanol and ethanol at its Khavda and Mundra SEZ facilities. The Khavda site has a land bank of 71,000 acres, which has a large-scale renewable deployment potential of 20 GW due to its high wind and solar resource potential.After the initial MoU, a more detailed ‘heads of agreement’ — pre-contractual negotiations for a commercial framework — was originally planned to be signed between May and September this year. But this is unlikely at this juncture.The Adani Group has, however, continued with the project work in Mundra on its own, aiming to complete a substantial part of the first phase of the integrated manufacturing ecosystem for ANIL by December.This involves 4.5 GW of solar module manufacturing capacity and 1.5 GW of wind turbine manufacturing capacity along with electrolysers, glass, aluminium frames etc. Analysts say over 5% of the total capex has already been incurred by Adani though the bulk of the work is scheduled for 2026-2028. Any binding agreement with Total is now expected only in 2024 or 2025 and the valuation and the overall commercial terms is likely to get altered as the French company is not incurring any of the greenfield project risks, they said.“We have 40 GW of land equivalent. We've been doing solar modules for the past five years. We know we will produce modules at 15 cents to 17 cents,” Robbie Singh, chief financial officer of Adani Enterprises, had told ET on January 22.Other than the green hydrogen project, Total has just over $3 billion of investments with Adani, including in gas distribution and solar projects, which it has played down as a small 2.4% slice of its total capital commitments.

morning.text:
Mumbai: Robust demand for office spaces has pushed commercial property leasing in the first three quarters of 2019 by 30% from a year ago, taking it closer to entire 2018’s performance and making sure that this year surpasses the peak touched last year.Driven by tech corporates — accounting for about a third of the leasing activity — office space take-up touched 47 million sq ft in the first nine months against entire 2018’s performance of 48.9 million sq ft, showed data from CBRE South Asia. With this, office leasing activity is now expected to touch its highest level ever, estimated to be over 60 million sq ft in 2019.Leasing activity stood at about 15.4 million sq ft during the quarter ended September, rising by nearly 23% on an annual basis. This was dominated by small- to medium-sized transactions. Small-sized transactions of less than 10,000 sq ft accounted for over 40% of the transaction activity in the quarter.
